title: The royal party and the Prince on Sonny's drums
summary: At a millionaire's party a royal prince played Sonny Greer's drums, and the band was received warmly.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, you didn't -- I don't think you went to France that first trip, did you?
I don't think so.

I don't believe so. But I know what you did do, if you can remember. Well, I was thinking about the Prince of Wales, but there was also the Prince George, who became King of England. He, too, was at a party. As you say -- you said some millionaire, or some magnate, some tobacco magnate or something.
Yeah.
Gave a big private party in his tremendous home.
Yeah.
Or estate, or whatever it was. And the Prince of Wales was present, right?
That's right.
And then, his younger brother, who became King George --
I don't remember him too much, but --
Well, I think one of them -- didn't one of them play some drums?
Yeah. The Prince of Wales.
Was it the Prince of Wales?
Yeah. He got on Sonny's drums and beat the drums at the party that night.
Did he?
He was always around. We used to see him quite often.
Did you?
Yeah.

Isn't that funny? Well, you know, I don't know if you remember that story, but there was a story about they were entertaining Duke or welcoming him or something, or he was at the bar or something, and the Prince of Wales asked Duke, 'What are you drinking? What are you going to have?' You know. And I think the thing was champagne, or a scotch and soda or something, and Duke said -- I think he said he'd have a pink gin or something.
(Laughter)
And the Prince of Wales said, you know, 'I'll have a pink gin, too.' I know Duke had some funny stories about things that went on. But they really had a very warm reception for the band, didn't they?
Oh, yeah. Palladium Theater, that's what it was.
Yeah.
We opened at the Palladium.
